options.label: One analyst is making random titration errors
The titrant has lost strength
The sample changed between the two titrations
The colour endpoint is biased in coloured water, so the split is a method endpoint problem, not analyst carelessness or bad reagents

inference.explanation: Each analyst is precise but they disagree, standards split the same way by method, and reagents check out. A coloured sample shifting a colour endpoint explains a precise but biased difference.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the endpoint bias?

options.label: Archived titrant standardization log
Archived certified standard results by both endpoint methods on coloured and clear water
Archived analyst training records

nextClue.explanation: Standards by method isolate bias from sample and analyst variation.

clueText.nc-a: Titrant standardized on target.
clueText.nc-b: The colour method bias appears only on coloured standards and samples.
clueText.nc-c: Both analysts are trained and precise.

tasks.prompt: A regulatory sample for nitrate came back at double the plant lab value, and the investigation finds the sample sat unpreserved over a warm weekend.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: The compliance sample was collected Friday, shipped Monday, and received warm with no ice remaining.
The plant lab split analyzed Friday read half the reported value, and its duplicate agreed.
The courier log shows the cooler spent the weekend in an unrefrigerated depot.
A holding study on the same water shows nitrate stable when chilled but shifting in warm unpreserved storage with biological activity.
Field blanks and the lab report QA flags show no analytical error at the compliance lab.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Warm unpreserved holding during the weekend delay changed the sample before analysis, so the result does not represent Friday water
The plant lab under reports nitrate by half
Nitrate truly doubled over the weekend at the plant
The compliance lab made an analytical error

inference.explanation: Plant splits and duplicates agree, compliance lab QA is clean, and the documented warm weekend storage plus a holding study reproduce the shift. That fits holding degradation over either lab being wrong.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the holding effect?

options.label: Archived plant lab calibration log
Archived compliance lab QA report alone
Archived chain of custody, cooler temperature record, and holding study results

nextClue.explanation: Custody and temperature plus the holding study connect handling to the shift.

clueText.nc-a: Plant calibration was verified.
clueText.nc-b: Compliance QA was clean but cannot speak to pre receipt handling.
clueText.nc-c: Warm held splits shift toward the reported value while chilled splits hold the Friday value.

tasks.prompt: Chlorine residual trending shows a sawtooth that exactly matches the analyzer sample pump cycle, while grab samples are steady.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: Grab DPD results at the analyzer tap are steady at 0.85 mg/L through the sawtooth period.
The sawtooth period equals the analyzer reagent and sample pump cycle time.
A worn sample pump tube was found flattened, starving the cell part of each cycle.
Replacing the tube in a trial removed the sawtooth and the trend settled at 0.86 mg/L.
Plant dose and actual residual control are verified steady.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Plant chlorine dose is oscillating in a sawtooth
The analyzer sample delivery is starving cyclically, creating a false sawtooth on a steady residual
The DPD grab method cannot see the real oscillation
Electrical noise is driving the trend pattern

inference.explanation: Grabs at the same tap are steady, the period matches the analyzer own cycle, a flattened tube was found, and replacing it removed the pattern. Dose oscillation would appear in grabs, and noise would not match the pump cycle so exactly.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the sample pump fault?

options.label: Archived analyzer trend, grab comparison, and pump tube replacement record
Archived chlorine dose log
Archived electrical inspection log

nextClue.explanation: Trend plus grabs plus the repair outcome is the complete test.

clueText.nc-a: Sawtooth vanished after the tube change with no dose change.
clueText.nc-b: Dose was steady through the pattern.
clueText.nc-c: Electrical checks were normal.

tasks.prompt: Flow totalizer reads 12 percent high against the reservoir drawdown volume over a week, while instantaneous rates look plausible.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: A drawdown test over a measured reservoir volume shows true flow 12 percent below the meter total.
The mag meter zero and span checks pass, but the totalizer pulse scaling was changed during a recent SCADA update.
Instantaneous rate from the meter matches a clamp on ultrasonic check within 2 percent.
Reservoir level sensors were verified by manual tape measurements.
No leaks or unmetered draws occurred during the test week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The mag meter element has drifted high
The reservoir is leaking the missing volume
A pulse scaling error from the SCADA update inflates totals while the meter rate itself is accurate
The level sensors are misreading drawdown

inference.explanation: Rate checks pass on two technologies and levels were tape verified, ruling out element drift and level error. The scaling change timing and the totals only error fit a totalizer configuration fault, and no leaks occurred.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the scaling error?

options.label: Archived mag meter calibration log
Archived drawdown test record and totalizer configuration change log
Archived reservoir leak survey

nextClue.explanation: Drawdown truth plus the configuration record pinpoints the scaling step.

clueText.nc-a: Meter calibration was on target.
clueText.nc-b: Totals corrected exactly when the old scaling factor was restored.
clueText.nc-c: Leak survey found no losses.

tasks.prompt: pH readings in the lab and online differ by 0.5 units on softened water, but agree on raw water and on buffer checks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: Softened water conductivity is very low, and the lab electrode is an old general purpose bulb with a clogged junction found on inspection.
A low ionic strength rated electrode reads the softened water 0.5 units higher, matching the online probe.
Stirring and longer equilibration move the old electrode reading toward the online value.
Both probes calibrate identically in standard buffers.
Sample temperature compensation was verified on both units.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The online probe has drifted on softened water only
Softened water pH truly differs at the two sample points
Temperature compensation is failing on one unit
The lab electrode junction is unsuited to low ionic strength softened water, so its softened readings, not the online probe, are biased

inference.explanation: Buffers agree, temperature compensation checks out, and a rated electrode plus equilibration behaviour both support the online value. Junction clogging in low conductivity water explains a matrix specific bias.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the electrode matrix effect?

options.label: Archived online probe calibration log
Archived sample point plumbing record
Archived comparison of both electrodes and a low ionic strength electrode on raw, softened, and buffer samples

nextClue.explanation: The three water comparison isolates the matrix effect by electrode type.

clueText.nc-a: Online calibration was on target.
clueText.nc-b: Both points draw the same softened stream.
clueText.nc-c: Only the old electrode on softened water deviates, across all replicates.

tasks.prompt: A series of E. coli positive results in one distribution area was traced to sample bottles from one lot with residual dechlorinating agent missing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: Bottles from the suspect lot show no sodium thiosulfate present in a lot check, while other lots test correct.
Positives cluster only in samples collected in that lot, across different samplers and days.
Resamples in correct bottles from the same taps are all negative, with residuals present at sampling.
Chlorine residual at the taps was 0.7 mg/L, enough to keep regrowth in an unpreserved warm bottle plausible in the lab holding study.
The compliance lab method and blanks are otherwise clean.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Unpreserved bottles let bacteria survive or grow after collection, creating false positives unrelated to system water quality
The distribution area truly had repeated contamination events
Samplers used poor technique in that area
The lab incubated the samples incorrectly

inference.explanation: Positives follow the bottle lot across samplers, resamples in good bottles are negative at the same taps, and the lot physically lacks preservative. Technique or incubation faults would not sort by bottle lot.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the bottle lot fault?

options.label: Archived bottle lot preservative check and resample results by lot and tap
Archived sampler training log
Archived lab incubation log

nextClue.explanation: Lot by lot comparison is the decisive QA evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Every positive sits in the unpreserved lot and every resample in good bottles is negative.
clueText.nc-b: Training records are current for all samplers.
clueText.nc-c: Incubation logs are normal.

tasks.prompt: Turbidity spikes appear in the SCADA trend at exactly midnight each night and nowhere else, with no matching plant event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: The midnight spike is a single scan value equal to the daily maximum register rolling over in the historian configuration.
The local meter display and chart recorder show no midnight spike on any night.
Grab samples at midnight on two nights read normal turbidity.
Correcting the historian rollover tag in a test removed the spike from the trend.
No backwash, flow change, or dose event occurs at midnight.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A real turbidity event occurs every midnight
The midnight spike is a data historian artefact, not a real turbidity event
The turbidimeter fouls and clears at midnight
A nightly backwash is missing from the logs

inference.explanation: Local display, recorder, and grabs all show no event, and the value equals a rollover register. Fixing the historian tag removed it, which confirms a data artefact over any process cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the historian artefact?

options.label: Archived midnight grab sample log alone
Archived historian tag configuration and parallel local recorder trend for the same nights
Archived backwash schedule

nextClue.explanation: Parallel records plus configuration show where the false value is born.

clueText.nc-a: Grabs are normal but alone cannot locate the data fault.
clueText.nc-b: The local recorder is flat at midnight while only the historian trend spikes.
clueText.nc-c: No backwash is scheduled at midnight.

tasks.prompt: Hardness titrations in the plant lab read consistently 15 percent high after a new EDTA lot arrived, while calcium by the reference method is unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment plant log. Steady flow unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and maintenance records are available for review.

evidence.label: Standardizing the new EDTA against a certified calcium standard gives a factor 15 percent off the label value used in calculations.
Recalculating the week results with the measured factor brings lab hardness into agreement with the reference lab.
Blanks, indicators, and analyst technique reviews are all clean.
The old EDTA lot restandardizes at its label value in the same review.
Raw and treated hardness by the reference lab are steady across the lot change.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Analysts began over titrating this week
Plant hardness truly rose 15 percent this week
The new EDTA lot strength differs from its label and was never standardized, biasing every titration until the factor is corrected
The reference lab drifted low

inference.explanation: Standardization measures the bias directly, recalculation reconciles both labs, and the old lot checks at label value. A true plant rise would appear in the reference results, which are steady.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the titrant factor fault?

options.label: Archived analyst observation log
Archived plant hardness trend
Archived EDTA standardization record for both lots and the recalculated results comparison

nextClue.explanation: Standardization plus recalculation is the complete QA proof.

clueText.nc-a: Analyst observations were satisfactory.
clueText.nc-b: Reference trend shows no real hardness rise.
clueText.nc-c: Corrected lab values match the reference lab within 2 percent for the whole week.
